blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: The seat insertion sits five levels deep (for / if / match / if / for / if / if), so a reader joining the project must hold every enclosing condition in mind to know when a seat is added, and cannot answer without the plan: why seats are only added to an existing account when its plan differs from the row's (`account.plan != row.plan` reads like a filter for plan changes, while the doc comment says the function returns the seats created), why a seat without `'@'` is silently dropped, and why a row with an empty email is silently skipped. The seat loop is also duplicated between the `Some` and `None` arms. Flatten it: `continue` early on an empty email, extract one helper such as `add_new_seats(db, account_id, existing_seats, &row.seats) -> Result<usize, DbError>` used by both arms, name the `'@'` test (e.g. `is_email_seat(seat)`), and give the plan-comparison and skip rules a one-line comment stating why — or, if the plan comparison is not intended, raise it with the developer, as it decides which seats get created. Behavior must not change in the refactor.
findings.title: `import` nests five levels deep and hides its rules in unexplained conditions
